subject: Creativity
title: Rapid Prototyping: Build to Think, Not to Ship
description: A quick win: understand Rapid Prototyping: Build to Think, Not to Ship.

hook.text: The first iPhone prototype was a block of wood with a paper screen.

buildup.text: Prototypes aren't products. They're questions in physical form: 'Does this size feel right?

discovery.text: IDEO's rule: 'If a picture is worth a thousand words, a prototype is worth a thousand meetings.

twist.text: The goal of a prototype is to fail fast. Each failure teaches something a meeting never could.

climax.text: Google's Sprint method builds and tests a prototype in just five days — answering critical business questions before.

punchline.text: Don't build to ship. Build to learn. Shipping comes later.

quiz.question: What is the primary purpose of a rapid prototype?
options: To learn and test assumptions cheaply

details.summary: Rapid prototyping builds quick, cheap, throwaway models to test ideas before investing in development. The purpose is thinking, not shipping. Paper mockups, cardboard models, and role-play scenarios expose problems in minutes that would take months to discover in production.
details.whyItMatters: Prototyping is the fastest way to learn what works and what fails. It shifts creative development from debating abstract ideas to testing concrete ones, dramatically accelerating the design process.
takeaways: Prototypes are built to learn, not to keep
Low-fidelity prototypes test concepts faster and cheaper than high-fidelity ones
The goal is to fail early and cheaply before committing resources

faq.question: What is the fastest way to prototype an idea?
faq.answer: Paper sketches and cardboard models can be created in minutes and tested immediately. For digital products, hand-drawn screens photographed and linked in a slideshow provide a clickable prototype without any code.

faq.question: How rough should a prototype be?
faq.answer: As rough as possible while still testing the specific question you need answered. Higher fidelity is only needed when you are testing details like visual polish. For concept testing, crude prototypes actually produce better feedback because users focus on the idea.
